title: perf: Skip `__replace__` in Specifier comparison if not needed
head: 0e88c2d78a5ee6cfeb37eef93c75f2b0fc5361c4

families.why: The new `_public_version` early‑return adds an attribute access (`version.local`) and a branch on every call. When the prospective version *does* have a local segment (e.g. "1.2.3+foo"), the condition fails and the function falls through to `__replace__`, so the extra check is pure overhead.
families.size_meaning: n = number of dot‑separated local identifiers ("+a.b.c…")
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    # n >= 1
    base = "1.0"
    # Build a local part with n identifiers: +a.b.c …
    local = ".".join(f"loc{i}" for i in range(n))
    version = f"{base}+{local}"
    # Use a simple specifier that triggers `_public_version` (>=, >, <=, <)
    spec = ">=1.0"
    # The harness calls Specifier(spec) and then .contains(version)
    # We return the arguments for the Specifier constructor; the benchmark
    # will later feed the version to .contains.
    return [[spec]]

families.family: Versions with many local version segments (and pre/post/dev segments) cause the new early‑return checks in `_public_version` and `_base_version` to evaluate several attribute accesses before falling back to `__replace__`. This extra attribute‑access overhead makes the new version slower for such inputs.
families.why: The added `if version.local is None:` and `if version.pre is None and version.post is None and version.dev is None and version.local is None:` checks add four attribute loads for every call when the version carries local/pre/post/dev parts. Real‑world pre‑release, post‑release, dev‑release or local‑version strings (e.g. "1.0.0a1.post2.dev3+local1.local2...") trigger those extra checks.
families.size_meaning: n = number of local segments (and optional pre/post/dev segments) in the version string; cost grows with n.
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    """Return a list of argument lists for Specifier; each specifier uses a version with 1..n local segments (and one pre/post/dev each)."""
    specs = []
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        # build a version like 1.0.0a1.post2.dev3+local1.local2....localN
        local = ".".join(f"local{j}" for j in range(1, i + 1))
        version = f"1.0.0a1.post2.dev3+{local}"
        spec = f">={version}"
        specs.append([spec])
    return specs

families.family: Specifier strings with a plain release version (no pre/post/dev/local parts).
families.why: The new early‑return in `_base_version` returns the original Version object unchanged when `pre`, `post`, `dev` and `local` are all None, avoiding a `__replace__` call. Plain release versions hit this fast path.
families.size_meaning: n = number of release segments (e.g. 1.0.0.0 …). Cost grows with n because the version string gets longer.
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    return [[f">=1.{'.0'*i}0"] for i in range(1, n+1)]

families.family: versions with pre‑release, post‑release or dev segments
families.why: `_base_version` now checks four attributes (`pre`, `post`, `dev`, `local`). When any of them is present the condition fails and the function proceeds to `__replace__`. The extra four attribute reads + boolean logic are overhead compared with the old unconditional `__replace__`.
families.size_meaning: n = number of dot‑separated release components before the suffix (larger release tuple → more calls to `_base_version` in `_compare_less_than`/`_compare_greater_than`)
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    # n >= 2 (need at least two release components for ~= to split)
    release = ".".join(str(i) for i in range(1, n+1))  # e.g. "1.2.3"
    # Add a pre‑release suffix so `_base_version` sees a non‑None `pre`
    version = f"{release}a1"
    spec = f"<={release}"
    return [[spec]]

families.family: Plain release versions without pre‑release, post‑release, dev or local parts (e.g. "1.2.3", "1.2.3.4"). For these versions the new early‑return checks succeed immediately and avoid the `__replace__` call, giving a measurable speed‑up.
families.why: The added guards return early when `version.local is None` (and when all of pre/post/dev/local are None). Plain release versions satisfy both conditions, so the fast path is taken.
families.size_meaning: n = number of release segments (e.g. "1.2.3.4.5"). Cost grows with the number of segments because parsing the version string is O(n), but the new fast‑path is exercised for every segment count.
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    """Return a list of argument lists for Specifier; each specifier uses a plain release version with 1..n dot‑separated segments."""
    specs = []
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        version = ".".join(str(j) for j in range(1, i + 1))
        spec = f">={version}"
        specs.append([spec])
    return specs

families.family: Specifier strings whose version part contains a local version segment (e.g. '+local').
families.why: `_public_version` now checks `version.local is None` before calling `__replace__`. Versions with a local segment miss the fast‑path and pay the extra attribute access plus the original `__replace__` call.
families.size_meaning: n = number of additional local sub‑segments (e.g. '+local.extra1.extra2…'). Cost grows with n because the version string lengthens.
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    return [[f">=1.0.0+local{'.extra'*i}"] for i in range(1, n+1)]

families.why: The `==X.*` wildcard syntax allows many dot-separated numeric segments. The new parser strips the full string, slices off the two-char operator, then strips the version part — copying the long segment list three times. The old regex captured the version in a single slice.
families.size_meaning: n = number of numeric segments before the .* wildcard
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    # ==1.2.3....* with n segments
    segs = ".".join(str(i) for i in range(1, n + 1))
    return [[f"=={segs}.*"]]

def make(n):
    # ==N.N...* with fixed-length segment N repeated n times
    segs = ".".join([str(42)] * n)
    return [[f"=={segs}.*"]]

def make(n):
    # ==001.002... with zero-padded segments before .*
    segs = ".".join(f"{i:0>3}" for i in range(1, n + 1))
    return [[f"=={segs}.*"]]
